items.title: Observing and Controlling Features in Vision-Language-Action Models
items.description:
￼
Marco Pavone

Associate Professor at Stanford University and Senior Director of AI at NVIDIA

Following
Can we steer a robot foundation model without retraining it?

Our new paper explores this question through control-inspired notions of feature observability and controllability in Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.

We find that state- and action-relevant information can often be linearly predicted from VLA internal representations—and that these representations can be steered at inference time to change robot behavior, without fine-tuning.

As an example, on a real robot, our approach increased the preferred handle-grasp rate from 14% to 74%, while adding only ~1% inference-time overhead.

The broader idea is that representation-level control could provide a lightweight interface for adapting robot foundation models to new preferences and constraints—without retraining.

Joint work with Hugo Buurmeijer Carmen Amo Alonso Aiden Swann

items.title: Open models lecture: ecosystem, debates, and future access
items.description:
My first open model lecture, covering all the many pieces that build the ecosystem, and the open questions/debates determining where it goes next.

How does distillation fit in?
How do we manage risks?
How do we see access to models changing in the future?

I'm excited to revisit these questions about every 6 months, to give a state of the union on the field.
